title: Godot IDE's overly eager, unsaved shader rendering can cause system crash with non-terminating loops
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducable in 4.5.stable ### System information Godot v4.5.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.7.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Mobile) - integrated Apple M1 Max (Apple7) - Apple M1 Max (10 threads) - 64.00 GiB memory ### Issue description Godot compiles and renders shaders in the editor while they are being written; without waiting for the user to save or indicate they are finished working on it. In a gdshader, I briefly made a non-terminating `while` loop, when copying a code block and editing it to cover another case. The editor eagerly tried to render the shader, before I had finished making the new code valid, and this crashed my entire computer, (see screenshot below). I worked around the problem by using a different editor to fix the shader, to avoid Godot from eagerly rendering it and crashing again. (And replaced the `while` loop with a `for` loop to avoid a non-terminating loop.) ### Suggestions / ideas - Avoid rendering work-in-progress code before the user is ready, e.g. - Wait until the user saves before rendering - Have a "rebuild button" - Have a timout for shader execution in the editor, to catch infinite loops and prevent crashes ### Steps to reproduce I don't really want to reproduce this error and crash my computer again. But here is how I think it can be done: - Create a new project or open an existing one. - Create any node that can have a shader, like a Sprite2D or ColorRect. - Assign a new ShaderMaterial to it, and in the material, create a new Shader. - In the shader editor, paste the following: ```glsl shader_type canvas_item; void fragment() { float r = 1.0; while(true) { r *= 1.0; // just incase compile skips loop otherwise } COLOR.r = r; } ``` ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) (See above, I don't want to risk crashing my PC by making a reproducer. Not much is needed to reproduce.)
